---
title: "Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) & Parallel Analysis"
output: 
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    theme: readable
params:
  k_factors: 3   # number of factors extracted in the EFA (run with 3 and 4)
---

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# Required libraries
library(psych)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(GPArotation) # Required for oblique rotations (e.g., oblimin)
library(here)

# psych runs parallel analysis simulations on several cores on macOS/Linux,
# which makes the random results change from run to run even with set.seed().
# One core gives reproducible results, identical to those obtained on Windows.
options(mc.cores = 1)

# Paths are relative to the repository root (instrument.Rproj).
# Input: polychoric correlations of the UXVis items, from step 03.
phase_dir  <- here("phase3-validation")
data_dir   <- file.path(phase_dir, "03_polychoric-correlations", "output", "uxvis-scales")
output_dir <- file.path(phase_dir, "04_number-of-factors", "output",
                        paste0(params$k_factors, "-factors"))
```

```{r load-polychoric matrices}
# Construct file paths
r_file <- file.path(data_dir, "polychoric_correlation_matrix_r.csv")
n_file <- file.path(data_dir, "polychoric_correlation_matrix_n.csv")

# Read the polychoric correlation matrix (r) and pairwise sample size matrix (n)
r_mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(r_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
n_mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(n_file, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))

# Representative sample size (median of pairwise complete observations)
n_sample <- median(n_mat, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Matrix dimensions:", nrow(r_mat), "items x", ncol(r_mat), "items\n")
cat("Representative sample size (median N):", n_sample, "\n")



```

```{r test of sphericity}
# 1. Bartlett's Test of Sphericity
bartlett_res <- cortest.bartlett(r_mat, n = n_sample)
cat("--- Bartlett's Test of Sphericity ---\n")
cat("Chi-square:", round(bartlett_res$chisq, 2), "| df:", bartlett_res$df, "\vert{} p-value:", bartlett_res$p.value, "\n\n")



# 2. Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) Measure of Sampling Adequacy
kmo_res <- KMO(r_mat)
cat("--- KMO Sampling Adequacy ---\n")
cat("Overall MSA:", round(kmo_res$MSA, 3), "\n")


# 3. Individual Item MSA Table with Qualitative Evaluation
msa_values <- kmo_res$MSAi

# Individual item MSA table
#kmo_items <- data.frame(
#  Item = names(kmo_res$MSAi),
#  KMO = round(kmo_res$MSAi, 3)
#)
#kable(kmo_items, caption = "Individual Item Measure of Sampling Adequacy (KMO)")


kmo_items <- data.frame(
  Item = names(msa_values),
  MSA = round(msa_values, 3),
  Classification = cut(
    msa_values,
    breaks = c(0, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00),
    labels = c("Unacceptable", "Miserable", "Mediocre", "Middling", "Meritorious", "Marvelous"),
    include.lowest = TRUE
  ),
  Status = ifelse(msa_values >= 0.50, "Acceptable", "Flag (< 0.50)"),
  row.names = NULL
)


# Render table
knitr::kable(kmo_items, caption = "Individual Item Measure of Sampling Adequacy (KMO)")

# Print warning in console if any item is problematic
low_msa <- kmo_items[kmo_items$MSA < 0.50, ]
if (nrow(low_msa) > 0) {
  cat("\n[Warning] The following items have MSA < 0.50 and should be evaluated for removal:\n")
  print(low_msa[, c("Item", "MSA")])
}


```

```{r parallel analysis}
  


if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}


pdf_path <- file.path(output_dir, "scree_plot_parallel_analysis.pdf")


pdf(pdf_path, width = 8, height = 6)



# 2. generating the plot in the pdf
fa_parallel <- fa.parallel(
  r_mat,
  n.obs = n_sample,
  fa = "fa",
  fm = "minres",
  main = "Horn's Parallel Analysis Scree Plot (EFA - MinRes)"
)

# 3. close pdf
dev.off()

# 4. Present in the screen
plot(fa_parallel, main = "Horn's Parallel Analysis Scree Plot (EFA - MinRes)")

cat("Number of factors suggested by Parallel Analysis:", fa_parallel$nfact, "\n")


```

```{r efa}
k_factors <- params$k_factors

efa_model <- fa(
  r = r_mat,
  nfactors = k_factors,
  n.obs = n_sample,
  rotate = "oblimin",
  fm = "minres"
)

# Console output suppressing loadings below 0.30
print(efa_model$loadings, cutoff = 0.30, sort = TRUE)

#======
# Test Promax rotation and check factor complexity
efa_promax <- fa(
  r = r_mat,
  nfactors = k_factors,
  n.obs = n_sample,
  rotate = "promax",
  fm = "minres"
)

# Inspect sorted pattern matrix and item complexity
print(efa_promax$loadings, cutoff = 0.30, sort = TRUE)





```

```{r factor Loadings, Communalities, and Uniquenesses}
loadings_mat <- unclass(efa_model$loadings)

# Construct data frame with Loadings, Communality (h2), Uniqueness (u2), and Complexity
loadings_df <- as.data.frame(round(loadings_mat, 3)) %>%
  mutate(
    h2 = round(efa_model$communality, 3),
    u2 = round(efa_model$uniquenesses, 3),
    com = round(efa_model$complexity, 2)
  )

kable(loadings_df, caption = "Oblimin - Factor Pattern Matrix, Communalities (h2), and Uniquenesses (u2)")

loadings_mat_promax <- unclass(efa_promax$loadings)

# Construct data frame with Loadings, Communality (h2), Uniqueness (u2), and Complexity
loadings_df_promax <- as.data.frame(round(loadings_mat_promax, 3)) %>%
  mutate(
    h2 = round(efa_promax$communality, 3),
    u2 = round(efa_promax$uniquenesses, 3),
    com = round(efa_promax$complexity, 2)
  )

kable(loadings_df, caption = "Promax Factor Pattern Matrix, Communalities (h2), and Uniquenesses (u2)")


```

```{r Export}
# --- 1. EXTRACT AND ORGANIZE FACTOR LOADINGS ---

print(1)
# Extract raw unclassed loading matrix
loadings_mat <- unclass(efa_model$loadings)

print(2)
# Convert to data frame
loadings_df <- as.data.frame(loadings_mat)

print(3)
# Identify the primary factor (highest absolute loading) for each item
primary_factor_idx <- apply(abs(loadings_mat), 1, which.max)
loadings_df$Primary_Factor <- colnames(loadings_mat)[primary_factor_idx]

# Extract maximum loading magnitude (signed)
loadings_df$Max_Loading <- mapply(function(row, col) loadings_mat[row, col], 
                                  seq_len(nrow(loadings_mat)), 
                                  primary_factor_idx)

# Append item-level psychometric diagnostics
loadings_df$Communality_h2 <- round(efa_model$communality, 3)
loadings_df$Uniqueness_u2   <- round(efa_model$uniquenesses, 3)
loadings_df$Complexity      <- round(efa_model$complexity, 2)

# Move item identifiers from rownames to a clean dedicated column
loadings_df$Item <- rownames(loadings_df)

# Sort items: First by Primary Factor, then by Loading magnitude (descending)
loadings_df <- loadings_df[order(loadings_df$Primary_Factor, -abs(loadings_df$Max_Loading)), ]

# Reorder columns for clean display in Excel/Sheets
factor_cols <- colnames(loadings_mat)
final_cols <- c("Item", "Primary_Factor", "Max_Loading", factor_cols, 
                "Communality_h2", "Uniqueness_u2", "Complexity")
loadings_df <- loadings_df[, final_cols]

# Round factor loadings to 3 decimal places
loadings_df[, factor_cols] <- round(loadings_df[, factor_cols], 3)
loadings_df$Max_Loading <- round(loadings_df$Max_Loading, 3)




if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Export sorted pattern matrix
write.csv(loadings_df, file.path(output_dir, "efa_factor_loadings_ordered.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")

# Export factor intercorrelations (Phi)
write.csv(as.data.frame(round(efa_model$Phi, 3)), file.path(output_dir, "efa_factor_correlations.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Export global fit indices
fit_indices <- data.frame(
  Index = c("TLI", "RMSEA", "RMSEA_90_Low", "RMSEA_90_High", "RMSR", "BIC"),
  Value = c(
    round(efa_model$TLI, 3),
    round(efa_model$RMSEA[1], 3),
    round(efa_model$RMSEA[2], 3),
    round(efa_model$RMSEA[3], 3),
    round(efa_model$rms, 3),
    round(efa_model$BIC, 2)
  )
)
write.csv(fit_indices, file.path(output_dir, "efa_global_fit_indices.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Files successfully generated in:", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n")

```


```{r export-ordered-loadings promax}
# --- 1. EXTRACT AND ORGANIZE FACTOR LOADINGS ---

# Extract raw unclassed loading matrix
loadings_mat <- unclass(efa_promax$loadings)

# Convert to data frame
loadings_df <- as.data.frame(loadings_mat)

# Identify the primary factor (highest absolute loading) for each item
primary_factor_idx <- apply(abs(loadings_mat), 1, which.max)
loadings_df$Primary_Factor <- colnames(loadings_mat)[primary_factor_idx]

# Extract maximum loading magnitude (signed)
loadings_df$Max_Loading <- mapply(function(row, col) loadings_mat[row, col], 
                                  seq_len(nrow(loadings_mat)), 
                                  primary_factor_idx)

# Append item-level psychometric diagnostics
loadings_df$Communality_h2 <- round(efa_promax$communality, 3)
loadings_df$Uniqueness_u2   <- round(efa_promax$uniquenesses, 3)
loadings_df$Complexity      <- round(efa_promax$complexity, 2)

# Move item identifiers from rownames to a clean dedicated column
loadings_df$Item <- rownames(loadings_df)

# Sort items: First by Primary Factor, then by Loading magnitude (descending)
loadings_df <- loadings_df[order(loadings_df$Primary_Factor, -abs(loadings_df$Max_Loading)), ]

# Reorder columns for clean display in Excel/Sheets
factor_cols <- colnames(loadings_mat)
final_cols <- c("Item", "Primary_Factor", "Max_Loading", factor_cols, 
                "Communality_h2", "Uniqueness_u2", "Complexity")
loadings_df <- loadings_df[, final_cols]

# Round factor loadings to 3 decimal places
loadings_df[, factor_cols] <- round(loadings_df[, factor_cols], 3)
loadings_df$Max_Loading <- round(loadings_df$Max_Loading, 3)


# --- 2. EXPORT ALL TABLES TO output/ ---

if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Export sorted pattern matrix
write.csv(loadings_df, file.path(output_dir, "efa_promax_factor_loadings_ordered.csv"), row.names = FALSE, na = "")

# Export factor intercorrelations (Phi)
write.csv(as.data.frame(round(efa_promax$Phi, 3)), file.path(output_dir, "efa_promax_factor_correlations.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Export global fit indices
fit_indices <- data.frame(
  Index = c("TLI", "RMSEA", "RMSEA_90_Low", "RMSEA_90_High", "RMSR", "BIC"),
  Value = c(
    round(efa_promax$TLI, 3),
    round(efa_promax$RMSEA[1], 3),
    round(efa_promax$RMSEA[2], 3),
    round(efa_promax$RMSEA[3], 3),
    round(efa_promax$rms, 3),
    round(efa_promax$BIC, 2)
  )
)
write.csv(fit_indices, file.path(output_dir, "efa_promax_global_fit_indices.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Files successfully generated in:", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n")

```
